section.title: Logistic and threshold models
section.p: Separable equations gave us exact formulas when the variables could be pulled apart. But the formula is not always the first thing we should look for.
the graph of f already tells a story. It tells where solutions rise, where they fall, and which equilibrium values attract nearby solutions.
The logistic equation is the best first example. It can be solved by separation, but it is often understood first from its phase line.

subsection.title: Carrying capacity
subsection.p: The rate is proportional to the current population. That can describe early growth, when resources are plentiful. It cannot describe growth forever.
A population in a fixed environment has limited food, space, or available hosts. The model should slow down as the population approaches a maximum sustainable size.

exercise.title: Why does logistic growth slow as it approaches a carrying capacity?

statement.p: The logistic equation multiplies the exponential factor rP by 1-P/K. In your own words, what story do those two factors tell, and why is pure exponential growth a good early approximation but a bad forever-model?

hint.p: When P is much smaller than K, the slowing factor is near 1. When P=K, growth stops because remaining capacity is gone.

subsection.title: Phase line
subsection.p: the sign of f(y) depends only on y. That means one vertical line can summarize the motion.
This vertical summary is called a phase line.

figure.caption: The logistic phase line shows how the equation pushes solutions along the P-axis.

subsection.p: The arrows tell us the long-term behavior.
For a population model, the physically meaningful domain is usually
The mathematical equation also has behavior for P<0, but negative population is not part of the model’s interpretation.

note.title: Phase line
note.p: a phase line marks the equilibrium values f(y)=0 and uses arrows to show where y'>0 and where y'<0.

subsection.p: A phase line is a compressed direction field. Since the slope depends only on y, the whole plane can be summarized on one vertical axis.

paragraphs.title: A threshold model
paragraphs.p: The logistic equation says that any small positive population grows. Some populations do not behave that way. If the population is too small, individuals may have trouble finding mates, protecting each other, or maintaining enough genetic variety. Below a threshold, the population may decline.

figure.caption: In a threshold model, the population must start above A to move toward the carrying capacity K.

paragraphs.p: This model has a different story from logistic growth.
The value A is a tipping threshold. Starting just above it and starting just below it lead to opposite long-term outcomes.

exercise.title: What information is compressed into a phase line?

statement.p: For an autonomous equation y'=f(y), a phase line marks equilibria and uses arrows to show rise or fall. In your own words, why can one vertical axis summarize the whole direction field, and what does that picture tell you before any formula is found?

hint.p: If the slope depends only on y, every horizontal row of the plane looks the same. The arrows already predict long-term approach or departure.

subsection.title: Stable and unstable equilibria
subsection.p: An equilibrium solution is a constant solution. But not all equilibria behave the same way.
The arrows near c decide whether nearby solutions move toward c or away from it.

note.title: Stable and unstable equilibrium
note.p: An equilibrium y=c is stable if solutions that start near c move toward c as t increases.
It is unstable if solutions that start near c move away from c as t increases.

subsection.p: the equilibrium P=K is stable. Solutions below K move upward, and solutions above K move downward.
The equilibrium P=0 is unstable. A solution that starts exactly at 0 stays there, but a solution that starts slightly above 0 moves away from 0.
the equilibrium P=A is unstable. A tiny change in the initial condition can change the long-term outcome.
The threshold A is not a resting place that attracts the population. It is a dividing line.

note.title: What stability means in a model
note.p: A stable equilibrium is forgiving: small errors in the starting value still lead back to it.
An unstable equilibrium is delicate: small errors in the starting value move the solution away from it.

subsection.p: This matters in applications. A population near a stable carrying capacity can recover from small disturbances. A population near an unstable threshold may not.

exercise.title: What is the difference between a stable equilibrium and a threshold?

statement.p: In the logistic model, P=K attracts nearby solutions, while P=0 does not. In a threshold model, starting just above or just below A leads to opposite futures. In your own words, what does stability mean for a model, and why is an unstable threshold a dividing line rather than a resting place?

hint.p: A stable equilibrium is forgiving of small errors in the starting value. An unstable one is delicate: nearby solutions move away, so the long-term outcome can flip.

warning.title: Model warning
warning.p: continues mathematically below P=0, but the population model does not.
If the population reaches extinction, harvesting cannot continue at the same constant rate. The physical domain P\ge0 is part of the model.

paragraphs.p: The logistic and threshold models show why a differential equation is more than a formula to solve. It is a field of tendencies. It tells what the system tries to do from each starting value.

The next class of equations has a different structure. It may include an outside input, such as salt entering a tank or money deposited into an account. The equation is not always separable, but the product rule gives it a way forward.

exercise.title: Why can a constant harvest create a tipping point?

statement.p: In P'=rP(1-P/K)-h, equilibria occur where the logistic growth curve meets the harvest line. In your own words, why is there a largest sustainable constant harvest, and what happens to the story if the harvest exceeds that value?

hint.p: The growth parabola has a maximum. If the harvest line misses that curve, there is no positive equilibrium, and harvesting exceeds natural growth. The model also stops making sense at extinction.
